message.content:
I don’t have live access to real‑time weather or pollution feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI (Air Quality Index) for Los Angeles at this moment.

**What you can do instead**

| Source | How it works |
|--------|--------------|
| **EPA’s AirNow website** – <https://www.airnow.gov/> | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code to see the latest AQI readings from nearby monitoring stations. |
| **AQICN app/website** – <https://aqicn.org/city/united-states/california/la> | Provides an up‑to‑date map with color codes (good → hazardous). |
| **Local news outlets** (e.g., *LA Times*, KABC-TV) often report on smog alerts during high‑pollution days. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities today, check one of those sites before heading out—especially if you’re sensitive to pollutants such as ozone (O₃), particulate matter (PM₂.5 / PM₁₀), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), sulfur dioxide (SO₂), or carbon monoxide (CO).

Let me know if you'd like help interpreting the numbers once you've checked them!
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in LA. We don't have real-time data; we can provide general info and suggest checking local sources like AirNow or AQICN. No tool needed.
